message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may hold a maximum of **one month’s rent** (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.). | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or certified mail) of any needed repairs.
• If repairs are not made within a reasonable time, you may withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate the lease (see below). | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withholding** | • If the landlord fails to fix a major problem, you may:
1. **Repair & Deduct**: Pay for the repair and deduct the cost from your rent.
2. **Rent Withholding**: Withhold a portion of rent until the issue is fixed. | • Keep receipts and document the problem.
• Provide written notice to the landlord before withholding or repairing. | | **Lease Termination** | • You can terminate a lease early if the landlord breaches the lease or fails to maintain habitability.
• In a month‑to‑month lease, you can terminate with **30 days’ notice**. | • Provide written notice (email or certified mail). | | **Privacy & Entry** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Fair Housing** | • Landlords must comply with federal Fair Housing laws and Texas Fair Housing Act. | • Report violations to the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Rent Increases** | • In a month‑to‑month lease, the landlord can raise rent with **30 days’ notice**.
• In a fixed‑term lease, rent can only be increased at the start of a new lease term. | • Review your lease for any rent‑increase clauses. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Deductions must be for:
1. Unpaid rent
2. Damage beyond normal wear & tear
3. Cleaning costs if the unit was left dirty | • Dispute any unjustified deductions by requesting an itemized list. | | **Eviction Process** | • The landlord must follow Texas eviction law: serve a **Notice to Pay Rent or Quit** (10 days) or **Notice to Vacate** (30 days) before filing an eviction action. | • Respond promptly to notices; consider negotiating a payment plan or settlement. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If the landlord violates your rights, you can:
1. File a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office.
2. File a civil action in small claims court (up to $20,000).
3. Seek mediation or arbitration if the lease provides for it. | • Keep all documentation (lease, notices, receipts, correspondence). | --- #### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease** – Understand the terms, notice periods, and any special clauses (e.g., pet fees, subletting). 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, and written records of the unit’s condition at move‑in and move‑out. 3. **Notify Promptly** – Report maintenance issues in writing; keep copies. 4. **Know Your Notice Requirements** – 30 days for month‑to‑month termination, 24‑hour notice for entry. 5. **Keep Receipts** – For any repairs you pay for yourself. 6. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you’re unsure about a lease clause or a landlord’s action, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local tenant‑advocacy group. --- #### Resources | Resource | What It Offers | How to Access | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Information on tenant rights, how to file complaints, and consumer guides. | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | Handles discrimination complaints. | https://www.tchra.org/ | | **HUD – Fair Housing** | Federal fair housing resources and complaint filing. | https://www.hud.gov/ | | **Local Tenant‑Advocacy Groups** | Free legal clinics, mediation services, and tenant education. | Search online for “tenant advocacy Texas” or check your city’s website. | | **Texas Small Claims Court** | Process for filing a claim up to $20,000. | https://www.txcourts.gov/small-claims/ | --- #### When to Call a Lawyer - The landlord refuses to make necessary repairs after notice. - You’re being evicted without proper notice or legal grounds. - The landlord is making unlawful deductions from your security deposit. - You suspect discrimination or harassment. - You’re unsure how to interpret a lease clause that seems unfair. --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, fair treatment, and clear communication from your landlord. Keep records, communicate in writing, and know the legal avenues available if your landlord violates your rights. If you need help drafting a lease or a notice, let me know!
